construct: Motilin is cyclically released from enteroendocrine cells in the upper small intestine during fasting and is associated with phase III of the migrating motor complex, producing strong propagating contractions that clear residual gastric and small-intestinal contents. Feeding suppresses the fasting MMC pattern.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Cyclic fasting phase-III migrating contractions of stomach and small intestine are associated with motilin; feeding interrupts the interdigestive MMC.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Several GI hormones affect motility, but secretin, CCK, gastrin, and GIP are meal/nutrient-related and do not define the fasting 90-120 minute migrating motor complex.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The periodic fasting motor pattern disappearing after a meal uniquely identifies motilin.
